guidePhoto.sous: The drawing starts from your photo: the clearer it is, the more the portrait looks like you. Here's what works, what to avoid, and the special cases.
guidePhoto.illustrationAlt: An original photo and the cartoon portrait drawn from it
guidePhoto.illustrationLegende: A sharp, well-lit photo is all it takes for a true-to-life portrait.
guidePhoto.bonsSous: No need for a photographer: a phone photo does the job perfectly.
guidePhoto.bon1Texte: Features, hairstyle and glasses are what make the likeness: they need to be clearly visible.
guidePhoto.bon2Texte: Front-on or three-quarter view shows both eyes and the shape of the face. In profile, half the details disappear.
guidePhoto.bon3Texte: Daylight, near a window or outdoors, gives true colours. Avoid harsh shadows on the face.
guidePhoto.bon4Texte: Zoom in on the eyes: if they stay sharp, it's perfect. The original file always beats a screenshot.
guidePhoto.bon5Titre: One photo per person is fine
guidePhoto.bon5Texte: Everyone doesn't need to pose together: a good photo of each person, taken separately, often gives a better result.
guidePhoto.bon6Texte: You can send up to 8 photos per order: one per person or pet, plus one for an outfit or a detail you care about.
guidePhoto.eviterSous: These photos give a less faithful portrait.
guidePhoto.evite1Texte: They hide the eyes, the most expressive part of the face. Regular glasses are no problem at all.
guidePhoto.evite2Texte: Motion blur or an over-compressed photo wipes out the details of the face.
guidePhoto.evite3Texte: A window or the sun behind the person leaves their face in shadow.
guidePhoto.evite4Texte: In a landscape or group shot taken from a distance, the face is only a few pixels wide.
guidePhoto.cas1Texte: One clear photo of each pet, ideally at eye level. Pick one where its coat and markings are easy to see.
guidePhoto.cas2Texte: A group photo works if every face is sharp and large enough. Otherwise, send one photo per person: we bring everyone together in the same drawing.
guidePhoto.cas3Titre: Don't have the right photo yet?
guidePhoto.cas3Texte: You can order now and send your photos later, using the upload link you receive after your order.
guidePhoto.faq1Q: Is a phone photo good enough?
guidePhoto.faq1R: Yes. Today's phones take photos that are more than detailed enough. Send the original file rather than a screenshot or a photo received through a messaging app, which is often compressed.
guidePhoto.faq2Q: How many photos can I send?
guidePhoto.faq2R: Up to 8 photos per order. One good photo per person or pet is enough; the others can show an outfit, a hairstyle or a detail.
guidePhoto.faq3Q: Do I need a photo with everyone together?
guidePhoto.faq3R: No. Separate photos work very well: each person is drawn from their own photo, then everyone is brought together in the same portrait.
guidePhoto.faq4Q: Can I send my photos after ordering?
guidePhoto.faq4R: Yes. After your order, you receive an upload link to send or add your photos whenever you have them.
guidePhoto.faq5Q: What if my photo isn't perfect?
guidePhoto.faq5R: Send the best one you have. You get a preview before the final version, and you can ask for changes.
